Definition: Adult social organization in Zhu et al. (2023), excluding juveniles and infants. Solitary: generally lives and moves alone; pair-living: an adult male and female associate for more than one year in a common home range; group-living: at least three adults live together with synchronized activities and interactions. Multiple states are retained. Pair-living does not establish genetic monogamy. Readable category or semicolon-separated combination of categories. Source-specific view; secondary compilation except five Data3 species explicitly reported as social observations in this study. Species-row references are not trait-specific.
